A new `MicroVm` component, streaming for SvelteKit, and fixes for sites with a base path and for accounts that encrypt SSM parameters. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

### ⚠️ Before you upgrade

- **`sst/aws/workflow` now uses `@aws/durable-execution-sdk-js` 2.6.0, and two errors have new classes.** A step that fails inside `promise.all` throws `PromiseCombinatorError`, not `StepError`. A failed `waitForCallback` callback throws `CallbackExternalError`, not `ChildContextError`. Update code that checks for the old classes. ([#62](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/62), [anomalyco/sst#7024](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/7024))

### New

- **`sst.aws.MicroVm` and the `sst/aws/microvm` SDK**, for [AWS Lambda MicroVMs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-microvms-guide.html): isolated, stateful sandboxes with their own HTTPS endpoint. Lambda builds the image from your `Dockerfile`, and a linked function starts MicroVMs with `microvm.run()` and calls them with `fetch()`. It supports VPC egress and `sst dev`, and deletes old image versions. ([#58](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/58))
  - For now every MicroVM has 2 GB and no lifecycle hooks, until the AWS provider supports them.
  - `sst remove` fails while MicroVMs from the image are running. Terminate them first.
  - A deploy role with limited permissions needs the Lambda MicroVMs actions, including `lambda:ListMicrovms`, `lambda:ListMicrovmImageVersions` and `lambda:DeleteMicrovmImageVersion` to delete old versions.
- **`sst.aws.SvelteKit` can stream responses.** Turn it on with `adapter({ streaming: true })` in [`@sst-community/svelte-kit-sst`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sst-community/svelte-kit-sst) 3.1.0, out with this release. It needs this CLI or later. Update the adapter with `npm install svelte-kit-sst@npm:@sst-community/svelte-kit-sst@3.1.0`. ([#40](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/40), [#76](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/76), [anomalyco/sst#6674](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6674))

### Fixes

- **A site with a base path loads its static files again**, instead of getting a 403 from S3. This covers Next.js `basePath` and SvelteKit's and Astro's `base`. ([#72](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/72), [anomalyco/sst#6980](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6980))
- **The Router takes a base path off the start of a request path only.** A request with the base text in the middle of its path, or `/administrator` on a site based at `/admin`, got the wrong S3 key. ([#75](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/75))
- **SST works where a policy encrypts SSM parameters.** Before, every command stopped with `invalid character 'A' looking for beginning of value`. With a customer managed KMS key, the role needs `kms:Decrypt` on it. ([#73](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/73), [anomalyco/sst#6856](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6856))
- **SSR sites stop right away in the 11 regions without Lambda function URLs**, instead of failing minutes into the deploy. Auckland is one of them. Spain (`eu-south-2`) works again. Sites without a server function aren't affected. ([#60](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/60))

### Examples

- The Astro examples use Astro 7, which needs Node.js 22.12 or later. Those that deploy with the adapter use `@sst-community/astro-sst`. ([#53](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/53), [#54](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/54), [#55](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/55), [#56](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/56), [#57](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/57))

### Also

- The docs site has a logo. The workflow SDK's tests load again ([#69](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/69)). The automatic review asks for a `Closes` line when a pull request fixes an SST issue ([#71](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/71)). A release that fails partway can be finished by re-running it.

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.19.0
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.19.0"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
